idiom_name: type Step<T> = done | more union narrowed by the driver
implementation_notes: TypeScript's contribution is the step type: a discriminated union whose discriminant lets the compiler prove that the driver only reads the value after narrowing, removing the convention-by-comment that untyped trampolines rely on. The driver and the mutually recursive functions are the same closure loop as JavaScript; the compiler adds exhaustiveness checking, so a new step case is a compile error until every driver handles it. Keep ordinary recursion while depth is bounded, and remember that the emitted JavaScript has no tail-call support.
pitfalls: The union is erased at runtime, so a single any-typed step factory (or a JSON-deserialised step) reopens the convention the type closed.
Closures allocate per step; passing an explicit state object into a step factory is cheaper when the state is large.
Compiling to ES5 makes generator steps fail or need downlevelIteration, so library code that must ship ES5 should stay with the union/closure form.

variants.name: Generator steps pulled by a typed driver stack
variants.idiom_name: Generator<T, T, Step<T>> steps with an iterative driver stack
variants.implementation_notes: Where the target is ES2015 or newer, the same pattern can be expressed with generators: a step function is a generator that yields its next step and returns the final value, and the driver keeps an explicit stack of iterators (never yield*, which nests frames inside the engine). TypeScript types the generator as Generator<Step<T>, T, T>, so the value returned by a nested step is typed when it is resumed. This is the shape effect-style runtimes use, and it makes suspension points explicit in the algorithm.
pitfalls: yield* delegates inside the engine and restores the stack growth the driver was meant to remove.
The generator's return type flows through the driver as the resume value, so an untyped any in the middle erases the chain's type safety silently.
Generators are lazy: the first next() call is required before the step does anything, so a driver that forgets it appears to hang or returns undefined.
